author: Edward McKinnon
title: Oklahoma man pleads guilty to federal wire fraud charge - NewsBreak
text:
By Edward McKinnon ,
6 hours ago
SALLISAW, Okla. (KNWA/KFTA) — A Sequoyah County resident could spend up to two decades behind bars after pleading guilty to wire fraud this week.
Johnathan Michael Hartman, 47, of Sallisaw, pleaded guilty to one count of wire fraud in the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Oklahoma on Thursday, according to court documents.
A federal indictment filed in January 2018 alleged that Hartman "devised a scheme to obtain money and property from the victim by means of materially false and fraudulent pretenses, knowingly, and with intent to defraud the victim," according to a Thursday news release from the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of Oklahoma.
Hartman was charged with wire fraud following an FBI investigation, the release states.
Charge dismissed for Springdale man accused of taking advantage of incompetent person By pleading guilty to wire fraud, Hartman could spend a maximum of 20 years in prison and be ordered to pay up to a $250,000 fine.
Case background
Hartman allegedly approached a resident of Pittsburg, Kan., in 2012 about investing in a restaurant based in Tahlequah, Okla., the indictment states. He is accused of falsely stating he would buy the restaurant and telling the alleged victim that they could invest in and own 20% of it.
Hartman is accused of subsequently telling the alleged victim he would increase their ownership stake to 25%. Hartman also had the alleged victim send him money to purchase items for the restaurant, the indictment states.
The indictment lists 22 money transfers between July 2013 and November 2013. Hartman originally faced 22 counts of wire fraud before pleading guilty this week to one count, according to court documents.
